title: PowerToys Peek takes longer to open than Photos

actions.label: Close as elevated Peek cold-start overhead

comment.body: The current evidence points to launch overhead rather than a new Peek defect. The attached report and the follow-up analysis both show Peek being started *non-elevated from an elevated PowerToys runner*, which adds extra startup work before the UI can appear. The same log window also shows the runner starting many other PowerToys modules. I would close this as expected elevated-launch behavior and keep the existing guidance: if possible, avoid running PowerToys elevated when you want the fastest Peek cold start, or open PowerToys once at sign-in so later Peek activations stay warm.

issue_context.summary: Peek feels slower than Photos on the first open because this machine launches Peek UI from an elevated runner into a non-elevated Explorer context, adding process-start overhead before the preview window appears.
known_information: The report is on PowerToys 0.100.2 with an attached bug report ZIP.
The bug report settings.json records `is_elevated=true` and `run_elevated=true`.
Peek logs show `Peek::enable()`, `Starting Peek.UI process`, and `Starting Peek non elevated from elevated process` before the UI appears.
A maintainer already explained that the runner was also starting many other modules during the same cold-start window.
inferences: The observed multi-second delay is tied to an elevated runner crossing privilege boundaries and competing with suite startup work.
There is no evidence in the issue or attached logs of a Peek crash, hang, or incorrect steady-state preview behavior after startup completes.
issue_context.analysis: This is better treated as an expected-performance explanation than as new bug-fix work. The issue already contains the relevant log-backed diagnosis, and the attached report corroborates it.
initial_investigation: Downloaded bug report 49787 and confirmed the elevated-runner setting in settings.json.
Confirmed the quoted Peek log sequence inside Peek/ModuleInterface/Logs/v0.100.2/log_2026-08-09.log.
Re-read the maintainer comment showing that non-elevated cold starts and warm reopens are materially faster on a comparable setup.

judgment.rationale: The attached logs and maintainer follow-up point to expected cold-start overhead from launching Peek non-elevated from an elevated PowerToys runner, not to a new Peek correctness bug.
evidence: The issue comment from daverayment quotes Peek log lines showing `Starting Peek non elevated from elevated process`.
The downloaded bug report contains the same lines in Peek/ModuleInterface/Logs/v0.100.2/log_2026-08-09.log.

The same comment reports sub-second cold starts and ~100ms reopen times when PowerToys is already running non-elevated, which matches a launch-mode/perf explanation rather than a persistent functional defect.
judgment.recommended_action: Close with a scoped explanation that elevated-to-non-elevated launch is the observed cause and that the current workaround is to avoid elevated runner sessions when fast cold start matters.

fix_assessment.rationale: Current evidence points to expected launch-mode overhead, not to a repository change with a clearly scoped bug fix.
